name: Deborah K. Ross

biography.background: Civil rights attorney; First Amendment and juvenile justice advocate; worked with Gov. Jim Hunt and Sen. Roy Cooper to overhaul NC youth offender system; practice included municipal bond law for infrastructure financing. Born Philadelphia, PA; grew up in Connecticut. Represents Raleigh/Wake County, NC.

electionStatus.primaryStatus: Democratic primary for March 3, 2026 canceled — uncontested

statedPositions.quote: supports creating a comprehensive public option for health insurance, expanding Medicaid in North Carolina, taking steps to reduce the high cost of prescription drugs, and implementing other reforms to ensure affordable and equitable access to care for every American
statedPositions.notes: Explicitly public option, not Medicare for All; supports lowering Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 60; opposes turning Medicare into a voucher program

statedPositions.quote: PBMs have acted as unregulated middlemen, driving up the prices of life-saving medications for patients — her bipartisan PBM Reform Act will rein in abusive PBM practices and take real steps to lower prescription drug prices
statedPositions.notes: Authored PBM Reform Act; passed House Jan 2026; also voted for IRA Medicare drug negotiation provisions

statedPositions.quote: Climate change is an existential threat. Deborah supports clean energy alternatives, opposes fracking, and fights to preserve North Carolina's environmental heritage.
statedPositions.notes: Campaign website characterizes climate as existential threat; consistent with LCV 99% lifetime score

statedPositions.quote: Offshore wind energy is one of the best resources in our toolbox to combat climate change and unleash the power of American clean energy. We must unlink harmful oil and gas leasing requirements from landmark clean energy provisions.
statedPositions.notes: Co-introduced CLEAN Energy NOW Acts with AOC; authored offshore wind moratorium repeal provision in IRA; consistently supports renewables over fossil fuels

statedPositions.quote: Offshore wind energy is one the best resources in our toolbox to combat climate change... my provision to overturn the previous administration's 10-year moratorium on offshore wind leasing in North Carolina and other states in the Southeast was included in the historic Inflation Reduction Act, but it simply was not enough.
statedPositions.notes: Actively pushing to streamline green permitting by decoupling offshore wind from fossil fuel lease requirements; introduced Nonrestrictive Offshore Wind (NOW) Act

statedPositions.quote: Wake County needs modern, efficient transportation options to match its continuing growth
statedPositions.notes: Announced $19.3M in transit funding for Raleigh from Infrastructure Act; led NC Democratic delegation calling for robust transit/rail funding; secured $176M+ for NC transit overall

statedPositions.quote: Federal housing policy should prioritize the housing needs of everyday Americans, not speculative profits
statedPositions.notes: Focuses on institutional investor accountability and government-side affordability tools; no specific zoning reform position found

statedPositions.quote: It simply prevents future sales of assault rifles — weapons not designed for recreation, they're designed for combat.
statedPositions.notes: Voted for assault weapons ban; voted for Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (2022); endorsed by Brady PAC and Everytown; former state representative who opposed concealed carry expansion

statedPositions.quote: Ross co-sponsored the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, which addresses policing practices and law enforcement accountability by lowering the criminal intent standard to convict law enforcement officers for misconduct in federal prosecution, limiting qualified immunity as a defense
statedPositions.notes: Former NC-ACLU director who successfully pushed state police to collect race-based traffic stop statistics in response to racial profiling; co-sponsor of Justice in Policing Act

statedPositions.quote: As NC ACLU director, she worked to overhaul North Carolina's system for dealing with youth offenders
statedPositions.notes: Long-standing rehabilitation orientation from ACLU work; introduced End Prison Gerrymandering Act (Feb 2026); South's first anti-racial profiling bill as state legislator

statedPositions.quote: voted against House Republicans' budget resolution that would authorize steep cuts in funding for Medicaid, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Head Start, school lunch programs, and more to pay for $4.5 trillion in tax cuts for ultra wealthy Americans
statedPositions.notes: Consistently voted to defend and expand Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security; supported ARP child tax credit expansion; wants to expand and strengthen Social Security

statedPositions.quote: driving investment in transportation and infrastructure projects and increase renewable energy options in pursuit of a cleaner, greener future for our children
statedPositions.notes: Voted for ARP, Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, CHIPS and Science Act, IRA — all major public investment vehicles

statedPositions.quote: Deborah supports public education for all, reducing class sizes, raising teacher pay, investing in early childhood education, alleviating student loan debt

positionConflicts.conflict: NC Medicare for All Coalition has urged her to cosponsor the Medicare for All Act of 2021 and subsequent cycles — no evidence she has done so. She supports a public option and ACA expansion, not single-payer.
sources: NC Medicare for All Coalition letter
positionConflicts.notes: Not a true conflict — she is to the center-left on coverage model. She supports public option, not M4A. This is a known gap between progressive base expectations and her actual position.

econ_safety_net.evidence: Voted for ARP, opposed SNAP/Medicaid cuts in 2025 budget, cosponsored Social Security Fairness Act, supports expanding Social Security and Medicare, cosponsors Raise the Wage Act

econ_public_investment.evidence: Voted for ARP ($1.9T), Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, CHIPS and Science Act ($280B), IRA; consistent record of supporting federal spending on infrastructure, R&D, clean energy

econ_school_choice.evidence: Campaign platform explicitly supports public education, reducing class sizes, teacher pay, free pre-K; no support for vouchers or charter expansion found; aligned with NEA/AFL-CIO endorsers who strongly oppose school choice. No direct anti-voucher vote retrieved — inferred from overall posture.

healthcare_coverage_model.evidence: Explicitly stated: supports comprehensive public option, expanding Medicaid, lowering Medicare eligibility age to 60; opposes Medicare voucher privatization; does NOT support Medicare for All

healthcare_cost_control.evidence: Authored PBM Reform Act (passed House 2026); voted for IRA Medicare drug price negotiation; explicitly calls out PBMs as 'unregulated middlemen driving up prices'

healthcare_public_health.evidence: Supports ACA individual mandate structure, Medicaid expansion, public health interventions. No specific vaccine mandate or public health measure vote retrieved; inferred from overall posture and party alignment.

housing_zoning_supply.evidence: No federal zoning legislation votes found — zoning is primarily local/state. Secured federal affordable housing appropriations for Wake County. No stated position on zoning reform (YIMBY/NIMBY).

housing_affordability_tools.evidence: Secured federal affordable housing funding; wrote letter urging FHFA/CFPB to investigate institutional investor impact on housing; stated 'Federal housing policy should prioritize the housing needs of everyday Americans, not speculative profits'

evidenceSummary.notes: Five-year House record (2021-present) plus 10-year state legislature record (2003-2013) plus ACLU directorship (1994-2002) provides exceptionally deep, consistent evidentiary base. Attendance rate 99.2% over 2,679 votes means nearly every position has a vote attached. Primary gap is housing/zoning (a local/state issue where federal records are thin). The only position nuance: she is public option, NOT Medicare for All — a meaningful distinction from the progressive left flank. Campaign platform for 2026 repeats 2024 positions with no new commitments found.
